Subject: MAP & procurement sequencing for Redwood

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Procurement and legal at NeuraHealth are trying to lock the evaluation/runway and understand the dependencies across MSA, DPA and the eventual order form so we can show a clean path to our CFO.

High-level asks from our side:
- Can you share a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that maps MSA/DPA/order form milestones to dates and owners?
- We need an estimate for how quickly Redwood can accept a clean MSA (assuming no major redlines) and the preferred sequencing for DPA vs MSA signature.
- Any required security artifacts (SOC2 report, subprocessor list) and target delivery windows.

Our proposed runway: 3-week evaluation (pilot), then procurement + legal to review contracts in parallel, target signature by end of month.

CC'ing James (legal) and procurement. If you can send a MAP + a short sequencing note (even a single sheet), that will help us build internal approval slides.

Thanks,
Olivia Park
Head of Procurement, NeuraHealth

Attachments: none

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear asks. See proposed MAP and supporting artifacts attached. Quick summary below and next steps.

Summary (proposed sequencing):
1) Week 0: Sign mutual MAP & statement of pilot scope (non-binding) — both parties agree on evaluation success criteria.
2) Week 1–2: Pilot execution. Redwood provides SOC2 summary, subprocessor list, and DPA overview.
3) Week 2: Legal review window begins for MSA (we recommend executing an MSA with an order form placeholder to avoid blocking the pilot).
4) Week 2–3: Parallel DPA finalization and security Q&A — DPA can sign as an addendum or as a standalone DPA; we can be flexible.
5) Week 3: Finalize order form (pricing & billing) and execute signature (MSA + Order Form; DPA either attached or executed concurrently).

Requested from your side: confirmation of legal redline owners and any internal signoff gates (security committee / procurement council).

I’ve attached: Redwood_MSA_v3-diff.pdf (high level diff), DPA_Summary.xlsx (topline), MAP-NeuraHealth-proposed.xlsx, orderform-draft.docx.

If that sequencing works, we’ll:
- Lock a 3-week MAP with milestone owners in the attached MAP spreadsheet
- Karthik (cc'd) will start a quick legal intake and flag any high-priority redlines
- Vanessa (cc'd) will coordinate pilot onboarding

Would love a confirmation of the legal contact who will own MSA redlines (James?).

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer GTM, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_v3-diff.pdf; DPA_Summary.xlsx; MAP-NeuraHealth-proposed.xlsx; orderform-draft.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-12T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: legal intake and sequencing notes for NeuraHealth (RDW-3691)

Stephanie — quick internal note following Steph's reply. High-level legal considerations and proposed sequencing: 

Topline legal checkpoints (likely to surface):
- SOC 2 Type II report (we provide summary + controls; full report on NDA)
- Subprocessor list and standard obligations (we can provide SSAE language + prior notices)
- Data retention / deletion window: confirm customer retention policy (default 30/60/90 days)
- KMS / key management: support customer KMS? (usually enter as a checkbox for Private deployments)

Sequencing recommendation (minimize blockers):
- Execute MSA with commercial terms + order form placeholder. This allows pilot to run while legal teams work redlines.
- DPA: can be executed as an addendum during the MSA review; if NeuraHealth requires it earlier, we can provide a binder DPA for immediate signing.
- Order form: finalize after pilot acceptance (so pricing/seat counts reflect pilot outcome).

Redlines that would materially affect schedule: any unusual indemnity demands, limits of liability changes, or custom data residency commitments. If those appear, we should escalate to the contracts lead and propose a 48–72h triage.

I’ve added a quick checklist to the MAP spreadsheet and flagged two items for Vanessa to confirm (pilot SSO window, SLAs expected during pilot).

-Karthik

Attachments: none (referencing MAP-NeuraHealth-proposed.xlsx)

Thanks — the sequencing makes sense. A couple of clarifications from procurement/legal: 
- James will own the MSA redline review. He prefers a single-redline window (3 business days for comments) to avoid multiple iterations.
- For DPA: we prefer the DPA to be in place before any production data is used. Pilot can run on synthetic or masked data while DPA is finalized. If Redwood can provide a binding DPA addendum within 5 business days, procurement is comfortable running the pilot in parallel with MSA review.
- Security artifacts: SOC2 summary + subprocessor list are required prior to pilot kickoff. If the SOC2 report requires NDA, please indicate so.

Proposed gating:
- Day 0: MAP signed (non-binding), SOC2 summary + subprocessor list delivered.
- Day 2–7: DPA redline window (James).
- Day 7–14: Pilot runs (masked data) — acceptance criteria to be captured in MAP.
- Day 14–21: Finalize MSA + Order form; signatures.

We’ll aim to provide internal legal comments within the 3 business day window once we receive the MSA redline.

Olivia
Head of Procurement, NeuraHealth

Attachments: Neura_PO_Template.pdf
